stories.title: leonardo-ai: Leonardo Ai for Windows 10/11. Generates images and artwork from text prompts using AI models, then refines results with inpainting, upscaling and canvas editing tools for concept art and design work
stories.body:
Leonardo Ai turns text prompts, sketches, and reference photos into production-ready images on your Windows desktop. It is built for designers, illustrators, game artists, and marketers who need consistent visual assets without a browser tab in the way. This page covers what ships in the Windows build, how to set it up, and how to get clean results from the first session.

Leonardo Ai is a desktop image generation studio. You type a prompt, pick a model and a style preset, and it returns finished images you can refine, upscale, or edit in place.

stories.title: Anthropic breaks below $83 IPO price
stories.body: Anthropic PBC shares traded below their $83 initial public offering price for the first time, wiping out gains for investors who piled into the artificial intelligence lab’s record-setting debut last week.

views.text: They have no future business model. Open-weight models and specialized distilations can be hosted in anyones datacenter where fierce competition will bring down prices. The current problem is the hardware scarcity and that the few big frontier providers snatch all the hardware at inflated prices while at the same time offer subsidized tokens below cost.
views.author: littlecranky67

views.text: It's such a bummer you can't buy options the day of the IPO. These massive valuations are nothing but an exit strategy for initial investors. Gone are the days of building a company and letting investors get in on the growth. Get a literally insane valuation, go public, dump your stock and run.

stories.title: Macdonald Book Shop in Estes Park, Colorado
stories.body:
Founded in 1928, this family-run shop claims to be the oldest bookstore in Colorado.

At Macdonald Book Shop, a cozy and beloved store in the Colorado mountain town of Estes Park, selling books began as a side hustle. J. Edward Macdonald bought a small log cabin in Estes Park in 1908 and opened a hardware and general store next door, with one corner full of books for sale. When he retired, his wife Jessica turned the parlor of their home into a proper bookstore, also selling magazines, stationery, and school supplies. That was 1928. Books have been the focus ever since. Over the decades, the shop expanded to claim more of the original house.
